output.answer: Yes. The most recent action is at GM Financial, General Motors' captive finance arm, which cut about 400 jobs globally, reported November 10, 2026, "to support operating performance." Earlier in 2026 GM laid off roughly 500-600 salaried IT workers (announced May 11, 2026), filed a WARN Act notice on Aug. 12, 2026 for 350 layoffs at its Lansing Grand River Assembly/Stamping and Lansing Regional Stamping sites effective Jan. 14, 2027 (tied to retooling downtime, with employees eligible for recall or supplemental unemployment pay), and eliminated the third shift at its Oshawa, Ontario truck plant in late January 2026, cutting more than 700 direct jobs. Separately, layoffs began Jan. 5, 2026 for more than 1,300 workers at Ultium Cells' Lordstown, Ohio battery plant, a GM-LG Energy Solution joint venture.
caveats: The most recent cut (400 jobs, Nov. 10, 2026) is at GM Financial, GM's captive finance subsidiary, not at the core automotive workforce; the Automotive News page was paywalled, so the 400 figure rests on the headline and caption.

The 350 Lansing layoffs are tied to retooling downtime for a $1.25 billion investment; GM said it anticipates recalling affected employees at the end of the retooling period, and affected workers may get supplemental unemployment pay equal to 74% of hourly wages under the GM-UAW contract.
The Ultium Cells Lordstown/Tennessee layoffs are at Ultium Cells LLC, a joint venture between GM and LG Energy Solution, not a direct GM payroll action.
Counts such as '500 to 600' IT workers and 'more than 700' Oshawa jobs are reported ranges/minima; GM declined to give specific details on the IT cuts.

passages.quote: GM Financial cuts 400 jobs globally 'to support operating performance'

The global reductions began Monday and will impact about 500 to 600 employees, largely in Austin, Texas, and Warren, Michigan, according to a person familiar with the plans who was not authorized to speak publicly about the layoffs. GM confirmed the cuts... "GM is transforming its Information Technology organization to better position the company for the future. As part of that work, we have made the difficult decision to eliminate certain roles globally."

General Motors says 350 workers will be laid off in January at its Lansing Grand River Assembly/Stamping and Lansing Regional Stamping sites, both in mid-Michigan. The details of the layoffs were related in a WARN Act notice filed on Aug. 12 with the Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity. The layoff date is Jan. 14, 2027.

Workers at the General Motors Oshawa Assembly Complex will report for the final third shift tomorrow, as the company eliminates more than 700 direct jobs with hundreds of additional jobs lost at supply chain companies.

key_facts.fact: GM Financial cut about 400 jobs globally 'to support operating performance'; GM Financial's Q3 net income was $487 million, down 17% from a year earlier.

GM filed a WARN Act notice for 350 layoffs at its Lansing Grand River Assembly/Stamping and Lansing Regional Stamping sites in Michigan, effective Jan. 14, 2027, tied to retooling downtime; GM anticipates recalling affected employees at the end of the retooling period.
GM laid off approximately 200 workers at its Ramos Arizpe, Mexico complex as ICE Chevrolet Blazer production ends in October 2026.
GM laid off about 500 to 600 salaried IT employees, largely in Austin, Texas, and Warren, Michigan; GM confirmed the cuts, saying it is 'transforming its Information Technology organization.'
GM eliminated the third shift at its Oshawa, Ontario Assembly Complex, cutting more than 700 direct jobs, after reporting over $12 billion in pre-tax earnings for 2025.

Layoffs of more than 1,300 workers began Jan. 5, 2026 at Ultium Cells LLC's Lordstown, Ohio plant (a GM-LG Energy Solution joint venture); WARN notices also covered 710 workers at the Ultium facility in Maury County, Tennessee, effective Jan. 5, 2026.
